subject: Accounting
title: Key Performance Indicators
description: A micro-lesson that makes Key Performance Indicators usable.

hook.text: A dashboard full of numbers means nothing if you don't know which ones matter.

buildup.text: KPIs are specific metrics that track progress toward a company's most important goals.

discovery.text: Financial KPIs include return on investment, profit margin, and revenue growth rate.

twist.text: Too many KPIs dilute focus. The best companies track five to ten that truly drive performance.

climax.text: Good KPIs are measurable, actionable, and directly connected to strategic objectives.

punchline.text: Measure what matters. Ignore the noise.

quiz.question: What makes a good KPI?
options: It's measurable, actionable, and tied to strategy
It only looks at past performance

details.summary: Key Performance Indicators are quantifiable metrics that track progress toward strategic objectives. In cost and management accounting, KPIs measure efficiency, profitability, quality, and resource utilization to guide decision-making.
details.whyItMatters: What gets measured gets managed. Without KPIs, managers rely on intuition instead of data, and organizations cannot objectively evaluate whether strategies are working.
takeaways: Effective KPIs are specific, measurable, and directly linked to strategic goals
Financial KPIs include ROI, profit margin, and cost per unit; operational KPIs include cycle time and defect rate
Too many KPIs diffuse focus—most organizations perform best tracking five to eight key metrics

faq.question: What are key performance indicators in management accounting?
faq.answer: KPIs are measurable values that demonstrate how effectively a company is achieving key business objectives. Management accountants design and track KPIs like return on investment, cost efficiency ratios, and budget variance to evaluate performance.

faq.question: How do you choose the right KPIs for a business?
faq.answer: Start with strategic objectives, then identify the metrics that most directly measure progress toward each goal. Good KPIs are actionable (teams can influence them), timely (measured frequently enough to respond), and limited in number to maintain focus.
